# PicoCalc Shapes

*README.MD file mostly generated by Anthropic's Claude AI because Thomas Dzubin hates documenting code.  LOL*

A small shape-drawing demo for the ClockworkPi PicoCalc, built on the
Raspberry Pi Pico SDK. Author: Thomas Dzubin.

Six filled shapes sit on the 320x320 LCD in two rows of three: a thin
rectangle, a square and a triangle across the top, then a pentagon, a
five-pointed star and a circle across the bottom. Each shape can be grown,
shrunk, rotated and coloured on its own, and remembers its own size, angle
and colour while you move on to another one.

The display driver only offers a solid rectangle, so everything else is
rasterised by the program: the circle as a stack of one-pixel rows, and the
other shapes through a scanline polygon fill that also copes with the
concave star. All the maths is integer only (fixed-point sine and cosine
from a table), so it needs no `math.h` and no floating point, which suits the
RP2040.

## Controls

| Key           | Action                                                          |
|---------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------|
| LEFT / RIGHT  | select the previous / next shape (a blue box marks the selection); in colour mode, step the selected shape's colour around the rainbow |
| UP / DOWN     | grow / shrink the selected shape (stops at 1x1 pixel)           |
| F1            | toggle between shape-select mode and colour-select mode         |
| F4 / F5       | rotate the selected shape 5 degrees counter-clockwise / clockwise |
| ESC or Q      | leave for the PicoCalc UF2 Loader menu                          |
| ~ (SHIFT + `) | reboot into BOOTSEL (USB drive) mode                            |

In colour mode a small arrow above the rainbow strip points at the exact
stripe the selected shape is drawn in. The status line under the strip shows
the selected shape's name, size and rotation.

Leaving asks the loader for its menu through the watchdog scratch registers
(constants in `loader_const.h`); if the program was flashed straight to the
chip with no loader installed it simply restarts, and on a PC it closes.

## Files

- `picocalc-shapes.c` - the whole program. The header comment block at the top
  is the design reference (drawing primitives, rotation, selection and colour
  modes, screen layout).
- `loader_const.h` - the values used to hand control back to the UF2 Loader.
- `CMakeLists.txt`, `pico_sdk_import.cmake` - firmware build config.
- `desktop/` - Desktop (SDL2) build for Windows and Linux: its own
  `CMakeLists.txt` plus a small shim of the driver API, so the same
  `picocalc-shapes.c` runs on a PC.
- `picocalc-text-starter-main/` - vendored copy of `picocalc-text-starter` (see
  Third-party below).
- `CHANGELOG.md` - notable changes, by version.

## Building

VS Code Pico extension (Compile / Run), or from a terminal with
`PICO_SDK_PATH` set:

    cmake -B build -G Ninja
    ninja -C build

Output: `build/shapes-<chip>.uf2` (`<chip>` is `RP2350` or `RP2040`, matching
the board). Flash by copying to the `RPI-RP2` drive; hold BOOTSEL on power-up,
or press `~` (SHIFT + backtick) in the app. The build also copies the `.uf2` to
the top-level folder as `shapes-RP2350.uf2` / `shapes-RP2040.uf2` (by board),
so both chips' builds sit side by side.

### Windows

From an MSYS2 UCRT64 shell with SDL2 installed:

    cmake -S desktop -B build-windows -G Ninja
    ninja -C build-windows

Output: `shapes-Windows.exe` in the top-level folder. SDL2 is linked
statically, so it is a single file with no `SDL2.dll`. `~` simply closes the
program.

### Linux

The same source builds on Linux with the SDL2 development package installed
(for example `sudo apt install libsdl2-dev`). Unlike the Windows build, SDL2 is
**not** linked in statically: the program links `libSDL2` dynamically, and the
build copies that library next to the executable as `libSDL2-2.0.so.0`, where
the executable finds it through an `$ORIGIN` run-path. Keep the two files
together.

    cmake -S desktop -B build-linux
    cmake --build build-linux

Output: `shapes-Linux` and `libSDL2-2.0.so.0` in the top-level folder.

## Third-party

[`picocalc-text-starter`](https://github.com/BlairLeduc/picocalc-text-starter)
by **Blair Leduc** (LCD, audio and south-bridge keyboard drivers) is vendored
in `picocalc-text-starter-main/` and used under its own license (see the
`LICENSE` file in that folder). One local change is made there, not in
upstream: in `drivers/fat32.c`, `get_next_free_cluster()` now advances its
search hint past the cluster it hands out, so a long sequential write to the
SD card no longer re-scans every cluster already given out and looks hung.
